title: After Labour: Human Position in an AI-Robotic World System

equations.section: 1. The Question After Labour
equations.text: human labour -> production -> wage -> claim on output
equations.meaning: The industrial political-economy chain linking mass participation to a practical claim on output, which the paper argues is weakening as its universal bridge role.

equations.section: 2.1 Readout in this paper
equations.text: Readout_(Q,O,c)(S) = z,  z != S
equations.meaning: A readout is a finite, declared representation of a system relative to a question, reader/measurement interface, and context; the representation is not the whole system.

equations.section: 5. Technology Block: Candidate Generation, Knowledge, and Embodiment
equations.text: Z_dot_t = v_t G_t - delta_Z Z_t,  0 <= v_t <= 1
equations.meaning: Minimal epistemic firewall: validated knowledge grows from machine candidate-generation capacity only through a domain-specific validation conversion rate, with decay.

equations.section: 5. Technology Block: Candidate Generation, Knowledge, and Embodiment
equations.text: K_like != K_validated
equations.meaning: Non-collapse: knowledge growth is never inferred directly from compute or benchmark (candidate-generation) growth.

equations.section: 5. Technology Block: Candidate Generation, Knowledge, and Embodiment
equations.text: B^RB_t = N^RB_t q^RB_t
equations.meaning: Embodied automation capacity as deployed robot stock times effective per-unit capability.

equations.section: 5. Technology Block: Candidate Generation, Knowledge, and Embodiment
equations.text: B_dot^RB_t / B^RB_t = N_dot^RB_t / N^RB_t + q_dot^RB_t / q^RB_t
equations.meaning: Growth-rate decomposition of embodied automation capacity into stock growth and per-unit capability growth; the capability term (per-robot growth) remains open/unresolved.

equations.section: 5. Technology Block: Candidate Generation, Knowledge, and Embodiment
equations.text: M_t = (K^M_t)^kappa (A^AI_t)^alpha (B^RB_t)^beta
equations.meaning: Machine productive-capacity index combining machine-specific capital, operational AI capability, and embodied automation capacity.

equations.section: 6. Labour Centrality, Not Labour Disappearance
equations.text: L_t = < L^task_t, L^income_t, L^bottleneck_t, L^bargain_t >
equations.meaning: Four-dimensional labour centrality: task-execution reliance, income importance, non-substitutable bottleneck role, and worker bargaining leverage.

equations.label: Labour-Decentering Proposition
equations.section: 6. Labour Centrality, Not Labour Disappearance
equations.text: Labour-Decentering Proposition [Open]. AI and robotics can reduce labour centrality without eliminating labour. Stable employment can coexist with falling bottleneck or bargaining centrality; high wages for some workers can coexist with a declining aggregate labour claim; and human-facing residual work can expand while scalable productive tasks migrate to machine systems.
equations.meaning: Boxed proposition separating labour centrality (task, income, bottleneck, bargaining) from raw employment counts.

equations.section: 6. Labour Centrality, Not Labour Disappearance
equations.text: rho = (sigma - 1) / sigma
equations.meaning: CES elasticity-of-substitution parameter for the human/machine production block.

equations.section: 6. Labour Centrality, Not Labour Disappearance
equations.text: s^L_t = (omega_H H_t^rho) / (omega_H H_t^rho + omega_M M_t^rho)
equations.meaning: Human labour-income share under the restrictive benchmark of competitive factor pricing.

equations.section: 7. The Claim Constitution: From Wages to Citizen Claims
equations.text: q_t = o_t + tau_t(1 - o_t) = 1 - (1 - o_t)(1 - tau_t)
equations.meaning: Combined broad ownership share and redistribution rate applied to machine-capital income not already broadly owned.

equations.section: 7. The Claim Constitution: From Wages to Citizen Claims
equations.text: Gamma_t = s^L_t + q_t(1 - s^L_t)
equations.meaning: Broad material claim on domestic output; a claim-accounting identity for the stylized model, not a welfare function.

equations.section: 7. The Claim Constitution: From Wages to Citizen Claims
equations.text: q^min_t = (Gamma_bar - s^L_t) / (1 - s^L_t)
equations.meaning: Citizen Claim Threshold: minimum non-labour conversion required to hold a target material claim as the labour-income share falls.

equations.section: 7. The Claim Constitution: From Wages to Citizen Claims
equations.text: D^rent_(i,t) = (Rent^(AI,out)_(i,t) - Rent^(AI,in)_(i,t)) / Y_(i,t)
equations.meaning: Net cross-border machine-rent drain for country i.

equations.section: 7. The Claim Constitution: From Wages to Citizen Claims
equations.text: Gamma^net_(i,t) = Gamma_(i,t) - D^rent_(i,t)
equations.meaning: Simple domestic effective claim after cross-border machine-rent drain: a country can automate locally while rents accrue abroad.

equations.section: 8. Ownership Accumulation: The Stock That Reproduces the Next Claim
equations.text: W^M_(i,t+1) = (1 - delta_W) W^M_(i,t) + r^M_t W^M_(i,t) + s^(M,cap)_(i,t) + T^cap_(i,t) - Tax^cap_(i,t)
equations.meaning: Minimal stock-flow equation for actor i's beneficial claim on machine-productive wealth: return, new saving/acquisition, capital transfers/inheritance, and taxes/dilution.

equations.section: 8. Ownership Accumulation: The Stock That Reproduces the Next Claim
equations.text: o_t = ( sum_(i in B) W^M_(i,t) ) / ( sum_i W^M_(i,t) )
equations.meaning: Broad-population ownership share used in (11), for a declared broad-population set B.

equations.section: 8. Ownership Accumulation: The Stock That Reproduces the Next Claim
equations.text: current redistribution != future ownership reproduction
equations.meaning: Non-collapse: redistribution today does not by itself determine how the ownership stock evolves; social wealth funds, pensions, cooperatives, or public ownership can raise ownership share without dispersing operational control.

equations.section: 9. Scarce Assets, Rent Burden, and Effective Material Claim
equations.text: B^scarce_(i,t) = (R^house_(i,t) + R^land_(i,t) + R^energy_(i,t) + DS_(i,t)) / Y_(i,t)
equations.meaning: Household/population rent-burden share from housing, land, energy, and required debt service.

equations.section: 9. Scarce Assets, Rent Burden, and Effective Material Claim
equations.text: Gamma^eff_(i,t) = max{0, Gamma^net_(i,t) - B^scarce_(i,t)}
equations.meaning: Effective material claim after unavoidable scarce-asset rent burdens.

equations.section: 9. Scarce Assets, Rent Burden, and Effective Material Claim
equations.text: machine abundance != low rent burden != effective material freedom
equations.meaning: Second non-collapse: gross transfers/dividends can rise while effective command over discretionary life stagnates if scarce-asset rents rise faster.

equations.section: 10. Aggregate Demand and Realization: Who Can Buy the Automated Output?
equations.text: AD_t = C(Gamma^eff_t Y_t, m_t) + I_t + G_t + NX_t
equations.meaning: Aggregate demand as a function of the distribution of effective household claims and marginal propensities to consume, plus investment, government spending, and net exports.

equations.section: 10. Aggregate Demand and Realization: Who Can Buy the Automated Output?
equations.text: chi^dem_t = min{1, AD_t / Y_t}
equations.meaning: Simple realization ratio of aggregate demand to output.

equations.section: 10. Aggregate Demand and Realization: Who Can Buy the Automated Output?
equations.text: Pi^M_t = chi^dem_t Y_t - Cost^M_t
equations.meaning: Realized machine-capital profit depends on both productive capacity and demand realization.

equations.section: 10. Aggregate Demand and Realization: Who Can Buy the Automated Output?
equations.text: Gamma^eff Y -> AD -> Pi^M -> W^M_(t+1) -> M_(t+1)
equations.meaning: Feedback chain: distribution affects realization, profit, wealth accumulation, and the next round of machine-capital accumulation.

equations.section: 11. Ownership Is Not Transition Power: Conversion Gates
equations.meaning: Counterfactual conversion-gate control of actor/gatekeeper j over transition e, based on best viability with and without j.

equations.section: 11. Ownership Is Not Transition Power: Conversion Gates
equations.meaning: Credible exit of actor i from gatekeeper j: access and exit are not identical.

equations.section: 11. Ownership Is Not Transition Power: Conversion Gates
equations.text: D_(i->j,t)(g) = sum_(e in E(g)) w_e(g) G^conv_(j,t)(e) [1 - X_(i,t)(e; j)]
equations.meaning: Actor-specific dependency exposure for goal g, differing from a concentration-only formulation by treating concentration as a possible upstream cause/proxy rather than the load-bearing variable.

equations.section: 11. Ownership Is Not Transition Power: Conversion Gates
equations.text: Concentration != G^conv != D
equations.meaning: Non-collapse separating market concentration, counterfactual gate control, and dependency exposure.

equations.section: 12. Relational Class Position in an AI-Robotic Economy
equations.text: C_(i,t) = < O_(i,t), G_(i,t), Gamma_(i,t), A^access_(i,t), X_(i,t), D_(i,t), R^rent_(i,t) >
equations.meaning: Relational class position vector: beneficial ownership, gate control, claim, productive access, credible exit, dependency, and net rent position; a stable class requires persistent clustering and institutional reproduction, not one observation.

equations.section: 13. The Political-Economy-to-Human Bridge
equations.text: c^(PE->H)_(i,t) = B^(PE->H)(Z_t; i, g)
equations.meaning: A named bridge mechanism (price, time, language, information, credit, permission, legal standing, identity, sanction, switching cost, network access, or institutional recognition) required to upgrade a political-economic relation into a claim about human agency.

equations.section: 13.1 Live possibility, defined here
equations.text: Pi^live_(i,t)(g) subseteq Pi^feas_(i,t)(g) subseteq Pi^phys_(i,t)(g)
equations.meaning: Nesting of physically possible, structurally feasible, and currently live options for person i and goal g; a live possibility is intelligible, discoverable, credible, and actionable, not merely legally present.

equations.section: 13.1 Live possibility, defined here
equations.text: Lambda_dot^live_(H,t) = lambda_1 B_t + lambda_2 X_t + lambda_3 P^plural_t + lambda_4 r^H_t - lambda_5 D_t - lambda_6 C^I_t - delta_Lambda Lambda^live_(H,t)
equations.meaning: Candidate dynamic for the macro-readout of breadth and corrigibility of live alternatives, driven by material security, exit, plural informational access, Human Return, dependency, and control cost; marked Open, to be removed if simpler measures explain the same outcomes.

equations.section: 13.2 Corrigible human agency, defined here
equations.text: A^corr_(H,i,t)(g) = max_(pi in Pi^live_(i,t)(g)) Pr^pi( R_g cap D_g cap X_g cap F_g )
equations.meaning: Task-relative corrigible-agency envelope: probability of jointly reading relevant differences, retaining attributable acceptance/refusal, causal enactment, and feedback/revision, over the live option set. Not a metaphysical free-will score.

equations.section: 13.3 Human Return, defined here
equations.text: R^return_(H,t) = < C_t, T_t, S^skill_t, A^alt_t >
equations.meaning: Delayed unaided return profile: Conceptual reconstruction, Tool selection, Skill execution, and Alternative generation after decisive AI assistance is removed; a normalized readout may be constructed under frozen criteria, without requiring CTSA as a validated scale.

equations.section: 14. Social Role After Labour
equations.text: S_dot^H_t = s_1 W_t + s_2 N_t - delta_S S^H_t
equations.meaning: Minimal dynamic for recognized social role/standing, driven by employment-based role provision and non-work role infrastructure (care, family, religion, civic activity, learning, arts, chosen work).

equations.section: 14. Social Role After Labour
equations.text: 1 = l_wage + l_care + l_learn + l_civic + l_leisure
equations.meaning: Time-budget identity; a fall in wage-labour time share is not automatically liberation or deprivation, direction depends on voluntariness, claim, recognition, capability, and live alternatives.

equations.section: 15. Social Reproduction: Productive Necessity Is Not Social Necessity
equations.text: H_dot^cap_t = f(Care_t, Health_t, Education_t, Nutrition_t, Community_t) - delta_H H^cap_t
equations.meaning: Candidate reproduction dynamic for a broad human-capability stock distinct from the productive labour input; machine systems may assist or intensify unpaid coordination burdens, sign left open.

equations.section: 15. Social Reproduction: Productive Necessity Is Not Social Necessity
equations.text: productive necessity of humans != social necessity of human reproduction
equations.meaning: Central distinction: humans can become less necessary to scalable production while remaining indispensable to the reproduction of human life, relationships, legitimacy, and culture.

equations.section: 16. The Human Systemic Position Equation
equations.text: P^H_t = [ (Gamma^eff_t)^theta_Gamma (A^corr_(H,t))^theta_A (Lambda^live_(H,t))^theta_Lambda (r^H_t)^theta_R (S^H_t)^theta_S (X^H_t)^theta_X ] / (1 + D^H_t)^theta_D
equations.meaning: Human Systemic Position: a typed audit index over effective material claim, corrigible agency, live possibility, Human Return, social standing, and credible exit, discounted by dependency; not a welfare utility function or validated cardinal scale.

equations.section: 16. The Human Systemic Position Equation
equations.text: P_dot^H_t / P^H_t = theta_Gamma (Gamma_dot^eff_t/Gamma^eff_t) + theta_A (A_dot^corr_(H,t)/A^corr_(H,t)) + theta_R (r_dot^H_t/r^H_t) + theta_Lambda (Lambda_dot^live_(H,t)/Lambda^live_(H,t))
equations.meaning: First part of the log-derivative decomposition of Human Systemic Position growth, into effective claim, corrigible agency, Human Return, and live-possibility growth terms.

equations.section: 16. The Human Systemic Position Equation
equations.text: ... + theta_S (S_dot^H_t/S^H_t) + theta_X (X_dot^H_t/X^H_t) - theta_D (D_dot^H_t/(1+D^H_t))
equations.meaning: Second part of the same log-derivative decomposition, adding social standing, credible exit, and dependency growth terms.

equations.section: 16. The Human Systemic Position Equation
equations.text: Y_dot_t > 0  =/=>  P_dot^H_t > 0
equations.meaning: Primary non-collapse result: rising aggregate output does not entail rising Human Systemic Position.

equations.section: 17. Abundance Without Agency
equations.text: AWA_t = < Y(up), Gamma^eff adequate, O^H(down), X^H(down), D^H(up), Lambda^live_H(down), A^corr_H(down), r_H(down), S_H(down) >
equations.meaning: Candidate Abundance-Without-Agency diagnostic state, used as a cross-check on (40): material abundance can coexist with structural dependence, a richer world can contain weaker humans.

equations.section: 18. Recursive Political Economy: Three Power Channels
equations.text: P_t = < P^econ_t, P^info_t, P^coerc_t >
equations.meaning: Typed power vector separating economic (ownership/rent/gate), informational (mediation/attention), and coercive (legally backed enforcement) power channels, which can align or diverge across actors.

equations.section: 18. Recursive Political Economy: Three Power Channels
equations.text: P^B_t proportional-to Gamma^eff_t A^corr_(H,t) Lambda^live_(H,t) X^H_t r^H_t
equations.meaning: Broad political capacity as a function of effective material claim, corrigible agency, live possibility, credible exit, and Human Return.

equations.section: 18. Recursive Political Economy: Three Power Channels
equations.text: P^E_t = P_E( P_t, G_dot^conv, D^H_t, 1 - Gamma^eff_t )
equations.meaning: Concentrated-system leverage as a function rather than a scalar identity, depending on the power vector, gate-power growth, dependency, and unmet claim.

equations.section: 18. Recursive Political Economy: Three Power Channels
equations.text: I_dot_t = F_I( P^B_t, P^E_t, state capacity, rules, shocks )
equations.meaning: Evolution of the institutional variable collecting ownership, redistribution, exit, interoperability, competition, and social-reproduction provision; no universal sign is imposed, three recursive loops can coexist.

equations.section: 18. Recursive Political Economy: Three Power Channels
equations.text: economic gate control -> rents -> political influence -> future gate control;  information control -> attention/interpretation -> rule legitimacy -> future information control;  productivity -> broad claim/exit -> agency -> collective rules -> broader ownership/exit
equations.meaning: Three recursive political-economy loops describing how technology alters rule-setting, which then alters the next ownership and gate structure.

equations.section: 18. Recursive Political Economy: Three Power Channels
equations.text: ownership != informational power != coercive power
equations.meaning: Non-collapse: the future is institutionally path-dependent, not technologically predetermined, and the three power channels must not be conflated.

equations.section: 21. What Humans May Actually Do
equations.text: labour-based claim -> human/citizen claim on social production
equations.meaning: The institutional transition required by a humane post-labour order: a new social constitution of contribution beyond scarce wage labour.

equations.section: 23. What Can and Cannot Be Forecast Now
equations.text: Omega_t = w_M(g_M - g_H) + w_D g_D + w_G g_G - w_q g_q - w_Gamma g_(Gamma^eff) - w_X g_X - w_R g_(r^H) - w_Lambda g_Lambda - w_H g_(H^cap)
equations.meaning: Normalized early-warning decoupling-pressure diagnostic combining productive/dependency pressure against institutional and human counter-response terms; persistent Omega_t > 0 is an early-warning condition, not a deterministic forecast.

equations.section: 24. Claim Boundaries
equations.text: concentration =/=> dependency =/=> agency loss
equations.meaning: Conditional non-collapse: under a pattern of low switching cost, robust interoperability, broad citizen claims, strong bargaining, and stable/rising Human Return, concentration need not imply dependency or agency loss.

equations.section: 25. Conclusion: From Productive Necessity to Human Membership
equations.text: candidate generation -> validated K/A^AI -> robotic embodiment -> M_t -> Y_t -> L_t -> s^L_t -> Gamma_t -> W^M_t -> o_(t+1) -> Gamma^eff_t -> AD_t -> Pi^M_t -> W^M_(t+1) -> {G^conv, X, D} -> human bridge -> {Pi^live, A^corr_H, r_H, S_H} -> H^cap_t -> P^H_t -> P_t -> collective rules -> next system state
equations.meaning: The standalone river developed by the paper, from candidate generation through to the next system state.

equations.section: 25. Conclusion: From Productive Necessity to Human Membership
equations.text: Gamma^eff Y -> AD -> Pi^M -> W^M_(t+1) -> {o_(t+1), M_(t+1)}
equations.meaning: The ownership-demand-production feedback loop closing the river.

equations.section: 25. Conclusion: From Productive Necessity to Human Membership
equations.text: {Care, Health, Education} -> H^cap -> {A^corr_H, r_H, S_H} -> P -> I_(t+1)
equations.meaning: The human-reproduction-political-rule feedback loop; a world-system regime is stable only if both feedback circuits reproduce themselves.

equations.section: 25. Conclusion: From Productive Necessity to Human Membership
equations.text: growth of machine productive power  versus  growth of broad human claim, exit, agency, and Human Return
equations.meaning: The critical inequality of the AI age, framed as a race between two growth rates rather than 'AI versus humans'.
